# Optional automatic Overleaf publishing

This uses Overleaf’s [Git integration](https://docs.overleaf.com/integrations-and-add-ons/git-integration-and-github-synchronization/git-integration) to pull a dedicated **public-safe** project. The public portfolio repo does not run this workflow or have access to the Overleaf token.

1. In Overleaf, create a separate public-safe résumé project. **Remove your phone number and any other private information from the source itself.** If you want the black bar, replace the number with a LaTeX rule such as `\rule{0.9in}{1.2ex}`. Never overlay a black rectangle on text that still contains your number. The template expects a one-page PDF compiled with pdfLaTeX.
2. In a new **private GitHub publisher repo you own**, copy [the template](overleaf-publisher.yml) to `.github/workflows/overleaf-publisher.yml` on the default branch. The template does not run if that repo isn’t private.
3. Set the repository variable `OVERLEAF_RESUME_PROJECT_ID` to the ID shown in the project's Overleaf **Git** integration URL. Set `OVERLEAF_RESUME_MAIN_TEX` only if the root file isn’t `main.tex`.
4. In the private publisher repo’s Actions secrets, set `OVERLEAF_GIT_TOKEN` to your Overleaf Git token and `PORTFOLIO_RESUME_PUBLISH_TOKEN` to a **fine-grained GitHub PAT restricted to `A-Sanil/A-Sanil.github.io`**, with Contents: Read and write. Overleaf Git access depends on your [Overleaf plan and Git token setup](https://docs.overleaf.com/integrations-and-add-ons/git-integration-and-github-synchronization/git-integration/git-integration-authentication-tokens); the Git token can have access to more than this one project. Don’t paste either token into chat, Git, or the website. If you don’t want to share that credential with a private CI runner, use the manual workflow.
5. Review the public-safe project and run the private repo’s **Publish public résumé from Overleaf** workflow manually. This **publishes** if the PDF passes checks. Verify the result at [resume.pdf](https://a-sanil.github.io/resume.pdf). Then set `PORTFOLIO_OVERLEAF_ENABLED` to `true` if you want checks roughly every 30 minutes. Scheduled GitHub jobs can run late. Remove that variable to pause scheduling.

Only `resume.pdf` is copied, staged and pushed. Source files and compile logs aren’t uploaded, and the workflow uses no force push. The phone-number check is a guardrail, **not** a replacement for keeping the source public-safe. Once scheduling is enabled, every compilable change from that project may go public. GitHub Pages will deploy the resulting commit through its existing branch setup; the separate narrowly scoped PAT is used because [a push using an Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` doesn’t trigger branch-based Pages builds](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/configuring-a-publishing-source-for-your-github-pages-site#troubleshooting-publishing-from-a-branch). Branch protections may require using the manual PR flow instead.
